entities.text: Rajana vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
on 3 September, 2019
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao

Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.4925 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A2 to A6 & A8 to A10 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.126 of 2019 of Krishna Lanka Police Station, Vijayawada, which was registered against them for the offences under Sections 273, 420, 188 r/w.Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006).

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 06.03.2019 at about 5:00 P.M., the SI of Police, on credible information raided at Rajiv Gandhi Park in Krishna Lanka, and registered the FIR, basing on the Mediators report prepared at the time of recovering the prohibited Gutkha and Pan Masala packets from the A6 and as per his confessional statement, the Police registered the same as a case in Crime No.126 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 & batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto filed on the report of the Sub Inspector of Police of Krishna Lanka Police Station.

Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore,
the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners under Sections 273, 420, 188 r/w.Sec.34 of IPC and Sections 58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, Interlocutory Applications pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
Rajana vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh.
